solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cadger is terrible person with shameful reputation

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters of the two words before it are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A sponger is condemned as a dreadful character with a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cadger is' looks like the start of a sentence, but both words are the fodder that 'terrible' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings shame on others is called a disgrace, as in 'he's a disgrace to the family'.

indicators.note: after places the gym lesson behind the party in the answer

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party or celebration
PE, physical education, is the school subject taught in the gym

explanation.surface: A fool turns up at the gym the morning after a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is informal slang for a stupid person, a dimwit.

parts.note: sh is the sound made to ask for quiet
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone listening quietly finds the call has been cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to clip or sever, as with wool sheared from a sheep.

clue.text: Communist is hidden — tracked down again

parts.note: red is the traditional label for a communist
something covered is hidden from view

explanation.surface: A communist in hiding has been hunted down once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rediscovered has been found again after being lost, so it has been traced a second time.

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it, used here as a verb
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A better person turns into a criminal boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective (a better individual), but it is the verb meaning to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era.

definitions.meaning: a group of people sharing a side in a dispute

explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes over-the-top, affected behaviour and also one side or party in an argument.

clue.text: Extremely foolish or insane, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborate or reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a thing is either very silly or plain mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as 'I think', but 'I' joins the fodder and 'fancy' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as stupid as a donkey, utterly silly.

clue.text: Heathen at home joined by one violinist

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, one outside the main religions
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A heathen staying in is joined by a companion who plays the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian virtuoso of the violin.

clue.text: At heart Adam's crazy, very much so

definitions.text: At heart Adam's crazy, very much so

indicators.note: crazy means deranged, so the letters of the three words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Deep down, Adam is thoroughly out of his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At heart' looks like an instruction to take middle letters, but it is part of the fodder: AT HEART gives A HATTER and ADAM'S gives MAD AS; 'very much so' says the madness is extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone completely insane, after the hat makers poisoned by mercury.

clue.text: Beg quietly, be out in front

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
to lead is to be ahead of the rest

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to plead softly while taking charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to implore or entreat earnestly.

clue.text: Supreme vegetable grower perhaps reaching a climax

definitions.meaning: a whimsical title for the top cultivator of a podded vegetable, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer into PEA KING, a champion grower of peas; 'perhaps' flags it as an invented example.
explanation.definitionFit: Something peaking is at its maximum, cresting at its high point.

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Artists notice their work has been hung for an exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentation is a show or exhibition of something to an audience.

definitions.meaning: a cracker is informal British speech for an excellent example of something

explanation.definitionFit: Crackers are splendid specimens ('a cracker of a goal') and the word also means crazy.

indicators.note: horrible means in a dreadful state, so the word before it is mangled

explanation.surface: An unpleasant neighbourhood is best left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is an area or zone of a country.

clue.text: Information English girl found in old book

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
sis, short for sister, stands for a girl

explanation.surface: Details about an English girl turn up in an antique volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament, so a book of great age.

indicators.note: inside means the zero sits within the word for refuge

parts.note: a haven is a place of refuge or shelter
O, the round figure, stands for nothing or zero

explanation.surface: Someone in a refuge has nothing on, an odd thing to wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something on is to be wearing it, as in 'have a coat on'.

clue.text: Point of view in Pakistan, certainly

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A firm opinion is held in Pakistan, of that there is no doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Pakistan' into the start of 'certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude held on an issue.

definitions.meaning: a ... liquid has not been diluted, the question mark showing a literal reading

explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated describes both intense effort and a drink or chemical that is undiluted.

clue.text: Like some type in select group

definitions.meaning: a size of typewriter type, twelve characters to the inch

explanation.definitionFit: Elite names a typewriter typeface and also the privileged top tier of a society.

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: dense means thick-headed or stupid

explanation.surface: A dim student fails to complete their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: A den is a private room for work or study, so studies are dens.

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

explanation.surface: An Asian celebration has been given a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern and oriental both describe things from the East, especially Asia.

indicators.note: running short means the word is cut back by its last letter

parts.note: WC, water closet, is a toilet

explanation.surface: Supplies in the lavatory are running low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests toilet paper, but it is the definition of a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Toile is a light cotton or linen fabric, often printed with scenes.

clue.text: Thus repeatedly appears to be mediocre

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is given twice over

parts.note: so means thus, in that way

explanation.surface: Something that keeps happening this way seems merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means only middling, neither good nor bad.

indicators.note: sounding means the word for stuffy is said, giving one spelt differently

parts.note: a stuffy room is airless, lacking fresh air

explanation.surface: A pompous aristocrat with no offspring sounds rather stuffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Without an heir, a person has nobody to inherit the title or estate.
